investigation.title: Remote Agent Creation Failing: Kubernetes Cluster Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All Checks
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed at 2026-07-02T09:43–09:51Z with an identical Kubernetes scheduler message: 0/6 nodes are available, 2 nodes report Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm and 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the pod never scheduled, no VM was provisioned, and the eval runner never received orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, or remoteState — leaving all four required evidence fields missing and both contract assertions unverifiable.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents swarm has exhausted its allocatable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the two nodes that match the pod's node affinity/selector. With zero schedulable capacity and no preemption victims available, every pod submitted for remote agent creation is stuck Unschedulable until the resource is freed or capacity is added. This is an infrastructure-layer scheduling failure, not an application code defect. No evidence of a user-traffic or production incident signal is present; the impact is scoped to this observability eval run.

possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the two affinity-matching nodes: both nodes show 'Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm' and preemption found no victims, meaning all allocatable VM slots are consumed by existing workloads or leaked pods.

Secondary — node affinity/selector mismatch reducing the schedulable pool: only 2 of 6 nodes match the pod's affinity rules; if those 2 nodes are also resource-exhausted, effective capacity is zero regardless of overall cluster size.
Tertiary — leaked or zombie remote-agent pods from prior eval runs holding kata.peerpods.io/vm slots without releasing them, preventing new pods from scheduling.
Lower probability — cluster-level quota or LimitRange on kata.peerpods.io/vm that was recently tightened, reducing the maximum allocatable count below current demand.

investigation.title: Remote Agents: All Three Checks Failing Due to Kubernetes kata.peerpods.io/vm Resource Exhaustion on Production Cluster
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api with identical Kubernetes scheduling errors: the 6-node cluster has only 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource, both of which are fully exhausted, while the remaining 4 nodes do not match the pod's node affinity or selector. Because no pod could be scheduled, the eval runner's createAgent call never completed, and the remote-agent-state check produced zero evidence — all four required fields (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) are missing.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler cannot place the remote agent pod on any of the 6 available nodes: 2 nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource are at capacity (Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm), and the other 4 nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity or selector constraints. Preemption is also unavailable — no lower-priority victims exist on the 2 eligible nodes, and preemption cannot help on the 4 affinity-mismatched nodes. The pod remained Unschedulable for ~142 s before the eval timed out, preventing createAgent from returning and leaving all required evidence fields unpopulated. This is an eval-detected infrastructure scheduling failure scoped to the remote-agents feature in production-api; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Creation Failing: Kubernetes Cluster Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All Checks
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed at 2026-07-02T09:43–09:51Z with an identical Kubernetes scheduler message: 0/6 nodes are available, 2 nodes report Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm and 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the pod never scheduled, no VM was provisioned, and the eval runner never received orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, or remoteState — leaving all four required evidence fields missing and both contract assertions unverifiable.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents swarm has exhausted its allocatable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the two nodes that match the pod's node affinity/selector. With zero schedulable capacity and no preemption victims available, every pod submitted for remote agent creation is stuck Unschedulable until the resource is freed or capacity is added. This is an infrastructure-layer scheduling failure, not an application code defect. No evidence of a user-traffic or production incident signal is present; the impact is scoped to this observability eval run.

Lower probability — cluster-level quota or LimitRange on kata.peerpods.io/vm that was recently tightened, reducing the maximum allocatable count below current demand.

possibleCauses: PRIMARY — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 eligible nodes: all available VM slots are occupied by existing workloads, leaving no capacity for new eval pods. Supported directly by failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-create, and sibling.remote-agent-state.

SECONDARY — node affinity/selector mismatch on 4 of 6 nodes: the remote-agent pod spec requires a node label or taint that only 2 nodes carry, meaning the effective scheduling pool is already small and any saturation of those 2 nodes causes total unavailability.

TERTIARY — transient cluster pressure or a concurrent workload spike consumed all kata.peerpods.io/vm slots at the time of the eval run, which may self-resolve if the occupying pods terminate. No historical run data is available (previousRunCount=0) to distinguish a persistent from a transient condition.

recommendedNextActions: Inspect the 2 kata.peerpods.io/vm-eligible nodes immediately to determine current VM slot utilization and identify which pods are occupying capacity.
Check for stuck or orphaned remote-agent pods in Pending or Running state that may be holding VM slots from prior eval runs or user workloads; terminate any that are no longer needed.

If VM slots are fully consumed by legitimate workloads, evaluate whether additional kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity (more nodes or increased per-node VM quota) is needed to support concurrent eval and production workloads.
Review the node affinity/selector configuration for remote-agent pods to determine whether the scheduling pool can be safely expanded beyond the current 2 eligible nodes.
Once cluster capacity is confirmed available, re-run the three remote-agent checks to verify recovery before closing this investigation.

Consider adding a pre-flight cluster capacity check to the eval runner that reports available kata.peerpods.io/vm slots before attempting agent creation, to produce a more actionable SKIP or WARN result instead of a timeout-based FAIL.
Note: this is an eval-level failure. No user-traffic or incident signals are present in the evidence. Do not escalate as a confirmed user-facing outage without additional traffic or incident data.

whatWouldDisproveThis: A successful re-run of remote-agent-runtime (or remote-agent-create) that produces a scheduled pod and returns all required evidence fields would indicate the scheduling failure was transient and has self-resolved.

Cluster node inspection showing that kata.peerpods.io/vm slots are not fully occupied on the 2 eligible nodes would suggest the scheduling failure has a different cause (e.g., a quota policy, a node taint, or a misconfigured resource request on the pod spec) rather than simple capacity exhaustion.

Evidence that only remote-agent-runtime failed while remote-agent-create or remote-agent-state passed in the same run window would disprove the shared scheduling dependency hypothesis and point to a check-specific defect.

A passing run of any remote-agent check immediately before or after this window with no cluster changes in between would suggest an intermittent scheduler issue rather than sustained resource exhaustion.

Cluster events showing the 2 kata.peerpods.io/vm nodes were cordoned, drained, or had their resource capacity reduced around 2026-07-02T09:45Z would shift the cause from exhaustion to a deliberate infrastructure change.
followUpEvals: Add a dedicated eval check (e.g., remote-agent-cluster-capacity) that queries the Kubernetes API for available kata.peerpods.io/vm slots on eligible nodes and warns when capacity falls below a safe threshold, providing early warning before scheduling failures occur.

Add a pod-scheduling latency eval that measures time-to-scheduled for remote-agent pods and fires a warning when scheduling latency exceeds a configurable threshold (e.g., 30s), catching capacity pressure before it causes full Unschedulable failures.

Add a node-affinity coverage eval that verifies the number of nodes matching the remote-agent pod's node selector/affinity is above a minimum (e.g., at least 2 healthy nodes), alerting if eligible node count drops.

Consider a post-run cleanup eval or teardown assertion that confirms eval-created remote-agent pods are terminated after each run, preventing slot leakage from prior eval executions from affecting future runs.
